newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to use mini-budget for economic plan-report.
newsitem.headline: France to use mini-budget for economic plan-report.

text.p: France's new Socialist-led government will not use decrees to implement its economic recovery programme but will stick to the usual practice of enacting a mini-budget, afternoon daily Le Monde reported on Wednesday.
The paper quoted acting Socialist party leader Francois Hollande as saying the possibility of using decrees was not on the cards.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said "that hypothesis (using decrees) was never considered and he was too respectful of the rights of parliament to think of taking financial measures without referring to the appropriate power, that is to say the National Assembly and the Senate," Hollande was quoted as saying.

On Tuesday, Le Monde said without citing any sources that in order not to disappoint voters hoping for swift change, Jospin was looking at the possibility of using decrees to reallocate spending credits without boosting public deficits.
